summary.oneLiner: Umiya Mobile delivered 47.5% YoY revenue growth to INR 8,084 Cr in FY26, driven by aggressive store expansion (100+ post-IPO) and a 73% B2B contribution, while successfully deleveraging (D/E 3.77x to 1.2x) via IPO proceeds. The core investment thesis rests on expanding EBITDA margins from ~1.9% to 3% by FY28 through operational leverage, higher-value accessories, and deepening penetration in underserved Tier 2/3 markets where offline 'touch-and-feel' dominates over e-commerce.

hero.oneLiner: Umiya Mobile delivered 47.5% YoY revenue growth to INR 8,084 Cr in FY26, driven by aggressive store expansion (100+ post-IPO) and a 73% B2B contribution, while successfully deleveraging (D/E 3.77x to 1.2x) via IPO proceeds. The core investment thesis rests on expanding EBITDA margins from ~1.9% to 3% by FY28 through operational leverage, higher-value accessories, and deepening penetration in underserved Tier 2/3 markets where offline 'touch-and-feel' dominates over e-commerce.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Smartphones contribute >96% of revenue. B2B segment contributes ~73% of total revenue (corporate incentives/bulk sales). B2C makes up the remainder. New categories (accessories, laptops, home appliances) being piloted to improve mix. Refurbished and buyback services currently 2-3% of revenue, targeting 10%.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A - Business model is high-velocity retail and B2B distribution with 20-30 days inventory turnover (DOS based).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Continued double-digit via new state entry (Maharashtra rest, Odisha, Chhattisgarh). Margin: Target 3% EBITDA by FY28 (up from ~1.9%). Order Inflow: B2B contribution target 35% in 2-3 years (vs ~27% currently). Capex: Funded internally; no external raise planned for next 18-24 months.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Geographic: Entering Bombay (Mumbai), Odisha, and Chhattisgarh in FY26; previously Gujarat, Maharashtra, MP. Format: Adding 100+ stores post-IPO; targeting 6-12 month break-even per new store. Product: Push into accessories, insurance (target 10% attachment), and refurbished phones to counter rising ASPs. Strategic: Migration from SME to Main Board in 3 years.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Current EBITDA margin ~1.8-1.9%. Path to 3% by FY28 driven by: 1) Operating leverage (platform ready, no incremental setup opex), 2) Higher margin combo offers/accessories, 3) Direct brand schemes (0.5-1% extra support on volume). Inventory managed via ERP with 20-day store/10-day warehouse stock; aging team targets <1-2% dead stock.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority 1: Debt repayment (completed via IPO). Priority 2: Aggressive store network expansion (Tier 2/3 cities). Priority 3: Working capital for inventory. Dividends: Deferred until expansion phase matures and pan-India presence is established.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, aggressive on expansion, pragmatic about margins. Emphasizes 'touch-and-feel' advantage over e-commerce in Tier 2/3. Transparent about deferred dividends to fuel growth. Strong focus on internal controls (ERP, Power BI) to manage scale.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) Margin compression if online price wars intensify despite management's 'price match' claim. 2) Execution risk in new states (Odisha/Chhattisgarh) with unproven demand. 3) High inventory risk in consumer electronics if demand slows (managed via DOS). 4) Dependence on B2B corporate spending cycles. 5) SME liquidity constraints until main board migration.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: 1) B2B is the dominant revenue driver (73%), not B2C retail, flipping the typical mobile retailer narrative. 2) 70% of transactions are via EMI/finance, driven by cashback arbitrage rather than affordability issues. 3) Marketing budget is deliberately shifted from traditional hoardings to digital and 'event-based' hype (e.g., bicycle giveaway in Indore) to avoid price wars. 4) Single store in Rajkot (Astron Chowk) generates INR 14-15 Cr/year, an outlier metric indicating high potential density.

challenges.body:
